stance.label: Short-term bearish, leveraged longs chased into the break-even wall; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: On a huge day for US stocks, BTC hit the $62–64K break-even wall and closed flat; leverage did the chasing, and those longs are tested next.
summary: Short-term bearish: US stocks surged, yet BTC was sold straight back after entering the $62,000–$64,000 break-even wall, with loss-taking spot coins sold into perpetual longs. Long-term bullish: even long-term holders are selling at an average 33% loss and total unrealized profit is down to 33.5% of market cap, in the historical bottom zone. A close above $64,000 would show the wall absorbed; a close below $58,525 is a new cycle low.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 12 straight closes below; the close needs +18.0% to get back above

overview.lead: Yesterday we wrote that this low had to get through the US stock open first; stocks then had their best day since April 2025, and BTC traded 1.9x the volume to close $44 higher.
points: Close $61,214, intraday high $64,520 and low $60,268 (Kraken), finishing in the bottom quarter of the day's range; the S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Nasdaq 6.51%.
Fear & Greed 11, day 11 of extreme fear; November is down about 21% so far, and the worst November since 2013 was 2018 at −37.0%.
Rates gave no help: Polymarket puts a December hike at 97.0%, and the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.63% sits 0.63 points above the Fed's upper bound.
No change in the exit framework or the market stage; 12 straight closes below the 200-day MA.

cycle.lead: Cheap has stopped getting cheaper: valuation gauges ticked up from the Nov 20 low and the bottom-zone readings are moving sideways, while not one trend light has improved.
points: The miner-capitulation signal in today's second finding sits on this page: one data source shows it and one does not, and this year already has 4 capitulation periods of 14 days or more (Bitview).
MVRV Z 0.26 and NUPL 0.129, above the 0.22 and 0.115 of Nov 21 (CoinMetrics, Nov 22); relative unrealized profit is 33.5%, day 10 under the 35% floor (Bitview).
The market stage is still bull, with 5 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA against the 30 the rule needs to leave it; only 1 of 6 evidence lights is on, exchange supply.
Long-term holders in loss 45.0%, against this cycle's high of 46.5% on Nov 20; the Tidemark bottom signal is 43.6, short of 50, and its cycle-low test runs to Dec 19.

market.lead: The down leg is intact: today's high stopped 4.8% short of the $67,627 line that would end it and was pushed back on heavy volume, so this candle did not improve the price structure.
points: The wall in today's first finding and this cycle's busiest price, $63,750, are the same zone, and the upper wick was left right there.
63 days since Sep 21 and −29.3% on a closing basis; deeper than 92% of this cycle's 12 down legs.
The close is −1.52 standard deviations in the short-term holder cost bands, with −1 at $66,113 (Bitview); only 3.6% of the past year's closes were lower.

The Sell Pressure Index is at its maximum for a 14th day with momentum at 0.11; this combination has occurred 20 times since 2012, with 12 higher after 90 days and a median further dip of 12% before the exit.

deriv.lead: Risk has changed sides: perpetuals on the three largest venues now all have longs paying, and estimated long liquidations within 5% below the close are nearly 4x the shorts above.
points: The buyers in today's first finding are here: perps on three venues were net taker buyers of 10,873 BTC, with $102M of shorts and $65.4M of longs liquidated (Coinalyze).
Weighted funding 4.78%, from 1.41% a day earlier; Binance flipped from −1.08% to 4.55% and Hyperliquid is at 10.59%.
Option protection cheapened for a second day: DVOL 52.3 from 55.4; 7-day implied vol is 4.7 points above 90-day, down from 8.3, and the 25-delta risk reversal is −8.0 (Deribit).

Estimated liquidation bands: 40K BTC of shorts at $64.6–68.1K above, about 9K BTC of longs at $53.7–55.1K below (several exchanges, an estimate); the book shows $249M of asks at $61,000 and $214M of bids at $60,000, all on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: Monday brought no spot: Coinbase selling is heavier than over the weekend, stablecoins keep going back into dollars, and the Asian bid that paid up at the weekend eased too.
points: ETF flows are worse than our chart shows: our source, CoinMarketCap, has Nov 20 at −$127M with IBIT missing; the complete figure from Farside and SoSoValue is −$669M, for $1.79B out on the week. Our 20-trading-day total of −$3.67B is therefore understated, and Nov 23 is not published yet.

Coinbase spot shows 4,820 BTC of net taker selling over 7 days, from 3,764 a day earlier, at the bottom of its range since August 2021 (Coinalyze); the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount is −0.011%.
Stablecoins $282.7B, down 1.5% in 7 days and $17.9B in 30 (DefiLlama); USDT trades at $0.9988, and its 7-day average discount of 0.156% is in the deepest 0.5% since data began in October 2022.

Apparent demand of −972K BTC is still inside the echo of the Nov 22–23, 2025 wallet move, a mechanical effect; exchanges saw 90K BTC of net outflow in 30 days (CoinMetrics, Nov 22), so coins are leaving exchanges while no bid shows up in traded volume.

onchain.lead: Yesterday we wrote that the peak of loss-taking had passed; today we correct half of that: daily realized losses are back at $1.3B, and the sellers include long-term holders at an average 33% loss.
points: The sellers in today's first finding are here: LTH-SOPR was 0.669 on the day with a 7-day average of 0.758, the lowest since Jun 29; 25.9% of realized losses over the last 30 days came from coins bought 1–2 years ago (Bitview, Nov 23).
Network realized losses were $1.32B on the day, against $329M on Sunday and the Nov 20 peak of $2.84B (Bitview); short-term holder capitulation is in day 14, with intensity down from 2.57 to 2.18.

Long-term holders realized $4.23B of losses over 7 days, from $3.88B a day earlier and a larger share of market cap than on Jun 30; their 30-day net position is −146K BTC, 111 straight days of net reduction (bitcoin-data, Nov 22).
By address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 76K BTC in 7 days while the 1K–10K tier shed 41K; the close is only 3.0% above estimated production cost (Bitview).

exit.lead: Nothing for the framework to do today; both upside conditions are more than 80% away.
points: 12 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $72,232, 15.3% under it; the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.414, with the 0.75 line at $110,776; the three top indicators read 8 / 6 / 36, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 22).

news.title: US stocks had their best day since April 2025: S&P 500 +4.73%, Nasdaq +6.51%, Nvidia +31.5%; the dollar index hit a 19-month high and BTC closed flat
news.read: On the best day for risk assets in a long while, BTC did not follow: our close is up 0.07%, and over the last 90 US trading days BTC already beat the S&P 500 on fewer than half of them. It follows on the way down and not on the way up because break-even supply sits overhead; today's first finding breaks down who sold. The dollar strengthened the same day and USDT's 7-day average discount widened to 0.156%. No change to the cycle view, but the near-term case loses "wait for stocks to steady" as a reason.

news.title: The 2-year Treasury yield rose above 4.72% at one point and the $69B 2-year auction stopped at 4.700%; the New York Fed president said "there is still more work to do", and futures almost fully price a 25 bp hike in December
news.source: Fixed Income News Australia (citing Reuters and Dow Jones), 2026-11-24
news.read: Our 2-year yield is 4.63% (FRED, Nov 23), 0.63 points above the Fed's upper bound; Polymarket has a December hike at 97.0%, up from 76.0% a month ago. Stocks can surge on one company's news, but rates have not eased for any risk asset. The 10-year real yield is 2.77% (Nov 20). This is funding backdrop and does not change the cycle view.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost $1.79B last week, the third-largest week on record and the fourth straight outflow; IBIT was $1.37B of it, with about $540M out on each of Nov 19 and Nov 20, both single-day records for the fund
news.read: This is worse than our chart shows: our source records Nov 20 at only −$127M, missing IBIT's $545M; Farside and SoSoValue both have the complete day at −$669M. On the complete numbers, outflows peaked on the two days price broke $60K and are not shrinking. ETF net assets fell from about $110B in mid-September to $71.35B. The largest fund is leading redemptions, and the near-term bid has not returned.

news.title: Strategy bought 457 BTC last week for $29.6M at an average of $64,898; in the same week it spent $211.8M buying back its own preferred stock, about 7x the BTC purchase
news.source: The Block, 2026-11-23 (SEC 8-K filed the same day)
news.read: The largest corporate buyer is still buying, but in small size, and the money goes to defending the preferreds first. Our data has it holding 851,305 BTC at an 18.9% paper loss, with an average cost of $75,446 above the close. 457 BTC is about one day of new issuance and does not move supply and demand; the MSCI index removal on Nov 30 is the next thing to watch.

news.title: BTC has fallen seven straight weeks, the second-longest streak on record (the longest was nine weeks in 2022); price is below the 200-week MA near $75,000, and traders price further hikes in January and March after December
news.read: Our swing measure says the same thing: the down leg since Sep 21 has run 63 days and −29.3% on a closing basis, deeper than 92% of this cycle's down legs. A long decline is not a finished one: the Sell Pressure Index has been at its maximum for 14 days, and that combination has seen a median further dip of 12% before the exit.

news.title: Miner Bitdeer sold all 281.1 BTC it mined in the week to Nov 20 and now holds none; hashprice hit a record low of about $26.20 per PH per day on Nov 21
news.read: This is the background to today's second finding. Our hashprice is $26.47, the breakeven for mainstream rigs is $66,605, 8.8% above the close, and difficulty is projected to rise another 9.9% on Nov 26. Miners are responding by selling coins and not by switching off: the 7-day hashrate is 11.3% above the prior week. It is a steady supply pressure measured in hundreds of BTC a day.

news.title: Deribit's Nov 27 monthly expiry has 112,323 BTC of open interest, about $6.76B notional, with max pain at $73,000; across all expiries the largest put strike is $60,000
news.read: Our reading today is 111,678 BTC, 25.9% of total open interest, with max pain at $72,000, far from the close, so most calls will expire worthless. Estimated dealer gamma is negative at $58,000 and $60,000, so hedging flows would amplify moves there (Deribit, an estimate); the expiry falls the day after Thanksgiving, when trading is thin anyway. This speaks to volatility and not to direction.

news.title: Oil fell to its lowest since late August: WTI settled at $80.17 and Brent at $89.37; the US president signalled more time for Iran diplomacy, and OPEC+ starts talks on 2027 output on Nov 29
news.read: Lower oil eases inflation and hike pressure, one of the few rate-side variables moving the right way; but the 2-year yield rose the same day, so the bond market has not changed its mind. The effect on BTC is indirect and changes none of our readings.

news.title: CFTC staff advisory: regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses may count BTC and ETH (haircut of at least 20%) and qualifying payment stablecoins (2% haircut) toward operating reserves
news.read: BTC gains one more use on the balance sheets of regulated US institutions, a long-term positive; it is staff guidance and not a rule, and it brings no new buying. None of our flow readings changed because of it today.

findings.title: Sold straight back from the $64K wall: loss-taking spot coins sold, leverage chased
findings.lean_why: Those selling into the wall include long-term holders at a 33% loss, and the buyers are leveraged longs paying funding; with no spot bid, those longs are the next group that could be forced to sell.
findings.what: The break-even wall held on its first test: on Monday price reached $64,520 intraday and closed back at $61,214, on 1.9x the previous day's volume (Kraken, Nov 23).
findings.why: Price has sat next to the thickest pile of short-term holder coins for two days, so by our rule this is a structural read; the question is who sold and who bought when price entered the wall. Start with how thick it is: short-term holders have 626K BTC in the $62,000 band and 486K in the $64,000 band, and long-term holders another 442K in the $62,000 band; short-term holders own 3.89M BTC at an average cost of $71,861, about 89% of it underwater (Bitview, Nov 23). Against a month ago, short-term holders have 233K BTC more and long-term holders 219K less, so coins are still moving toward short-term holders. There are two groups of sellers. The first is short-term holders: STH-SOPR is 0.983, below 1 for 18 days, with 13,201 BTC of realized losses on the day against 2,352 BTC of profits (CheckOnChain). The second is long-term holders: LTH-SOPR was 0.669 on the day, an average 33% loss on what they sold, and its 7-day average of 0.758 is the lowest since Jun 29; the network realized $1.32B of losses that day, and 25.9% of the last 30 days' realized losses came from coins bought 1–2 years ago (Bitview). Coin movement points the same way: 610K BTC changed price band in 7 days, of which 440K had a cost above the 7-day high and moved at a loss; the largest outflows were from the $64,000 and $65,000 bands and the largest inflow was 210K BTC into the $61,000 band (Bitview; an on-chain move is not always a trade). The buyers were in derivatives: perps on three venues were net taker buyers of 10,873 BTC while spot on three venues was a net seller of 1,188 BTC; $102M of shorts were liquidated, and weighted funding rose from 1.41% to 4.78% with Binance flipping from negative to positive (Coinalyze). Spot did not show up: Coinbase's 7-day net taker selling grew from 3,764 to 4,820 BTC, and the latest complete ETF day, Nov 20, was still an outflow. The estimated part: short-term holders of 30 days ago have moved 1.2M BTC since (an estimate; the total differs from actual by 0.6%); what needs no model is that coins above $88,000 fell by 125K BTC in 30 days.
findings.alt: The other path is that this was only a first probe: each test of the same wall clears out a batch of trapped holders, and today's $1.32B of realized losses is itself part of working through it. Spot tells the two apart: Coinbase's 7-day net taker flow turning positive and a close above today's high of $64,520 would show the break-even supply being absorbed. Data limits: LTH-SOPR is value-weighted, so one large move of very old coins can pull a single day down, and per-UTXO data cannot separate internal transfers; taker buying in perps includes short covering; funding is a one-day reading.
findings.history: After short-term holders are broadly underwater, price has usually been higher 30 days later, often after another leg down first. Short-term holders in loss has risen above 60% 16 times since 2015, with 12 higher after 30 days and a median of +8.4% (Bitview). The LTH-SOPR 7-day average has reached the bottom 2% of its one-year range 6 times since late 2023, with a 30-day median of −4.0%, worse than the +2.6% for any given day.
findings.so: What changed is who carries the risk: yesterday we wrote that perps pushed price up, and today those longs pay more funding and bought right under the wall, with estimated long liquidations within 5% below the close nearly 4x the shorts above. What did not change is the long-term picture: sellers are taking losses of a rare size, valuation is in the bottom zone, and neither the market stage nor the exit framework moved.
findings.next: By Nov 30: a close above $64,520 would mean Monday's selling was absorbed and this read is refuted; a day with more than $200M of long liquidations would mean the leverage that chased has been flushed.

findings.title: Miner capitulation flagged by a hair: hashrate rose 11% this week; the strain is costs
findings.lean_why: Miners have not switched off, yet their costs are about to rise another 9.9%; with the close below the breakeven of mainstream rigs, the source of inventory selling is still there.
findings.what: Hash Ribbons flagged miner capitulation today, by a margin of 0.03%: the 30-day hashrate average is 1,009.3 EH/s against a 60-day average of 1,009.6 (mempool.space, Nov 23).
findings.why: Start with which side is moving. Capitulation is defined as the 30-day average falling below the 60-day, meaning miners are switching off; the situation now is the reverse, with the 7-day average hashrate at 1,046 EH/s, 11.3% above the prior week, and the 30-day average simply yet to catch up. A second source disagrees with the signal: on Bitview's data the ratio is 1.0004, not below 1, and the Hash Ribbons chart on the site uses that series. The strain on miners is on the cost side: difficulty is projected to rise 9.9% on Nov 26, hashprice is $26.47 per PH per day, and the breakeven for mainstream rigs (20 J/TH at $0.06 power) is $66,605, 8.8% above the close; the close is only 3.0% above estimated production cost (Bitview). The Nov 20 news of a lender selling a miner's pledged coins and of MARA selling 13.6K BTC in six weeks belongs to this backdrop.
findings.alt: The other path is a real capitulation: hashrate turns down after the difficulty increase and the ratio heads below 0.99, at which point miners are switching off and inventory selling would grow. Data limits: hashrate is an estimate inferred from block times with large daily error; the two sources differ by 0.07%, and either could flip within days.
findings.history: This signal is no longer rare this year, and its link to price is weaker than it used to be. There have been 4 capitulation periods of 14 days or more this year (Bitview). For the original buy signal after capitulation ends, all 9 cases before 2021 were higher a year later; of the 5 since 2021 with a full year of data, only 3 were higher, with a median of +25%, about the same as buying on any day in that span.
findings.so: Little changed: the light is on, but miners have not switched off, so it cannot serve as bottom evidence. What did not change is the supply-side strain: the close is below the breakeven of mainstream rigs, and difficulty rises another 9.9% in two days.
findings.next: By Nov 30: the 30-day hashrate average rising above 1,015 EH/s would mean hashrate is still growing and the signal was a hairline cross; the 90-day low of the ratio falling below 0.99 would mean miners have really begun to switch off.

followups.title: First hurdle at $62–64K: underwater short-term coins wait, and perps did the buying
followups.say: Price entered the wall with an intraday high of $64,520 and closed back at $61,214; neither a close above $64,000 nor one below $60,000 has happened. Deadline Nov 29.

research.summary: Two new issues came out on Nov 23, Glassnode's Market Pulse Week 48 and Bitfinex Alpha; both describe larger ETF outflows and long-term holders joining the sellers, in line with our view that the bid has not returned. There is no Week On-chain newer than Nov 17.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 48
items.points: ETF outflows of $1.7B on the week, the heaviest since early July, with ETF holders' MVRV down to 0.97; futures open interest fell 12% to $29.3B, the lowest since early March; 25-delta skew rose to 17.4%, the highest since mid-July; supply in profit 47.3% and realized cap monthly change −0.93%.
items.meaning: Same direction as our data: the bid is leaving, protection is dearer and leverage was flushed. The difference is today: our open interest is down only 1.6% in 7 days and funding is up to 4.78%, so leverage is already coming back. Its realized cap monthly change is −0.93% against our −1.52%; the definitions differ and the two are not subtracted.

items.title: What Comes Next After a New Cycle Low?
items.points: The Nov 21 low of $55,501 was the lowest since September 2024, after seven straight weekly declines; resistance at $61,300 and the short-term holder cost basis of $72,720, realized price $53,200; ETF outflows of $1.25B for Nov 16–20; base case is a $56,800–$64,900 range into the Nov 27 expiry, with risk skewed to a retest of $55,501.
items.meaning: The top of its range, $64,900, is close to the top of our break-even wall, and Monday's high stopped just under it. Our short-term holder cost is $72,601 and realized price $53,149 (Bitview), nearly identical. Its weekly ETF outflow is smaller than SoSoValue's $1.79B; the sources are not reconciled.

items.title: 10x Weekly Crypto Kickoff: $57,300 Reached. Trust the Bounce, but for How Long?
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: its $57,300 target was reached, a tactical bounce is possible, but the primary trend is still bearish; its BTC trend model turned bearish on Oct 22.
items.meaning: Same direction as our near-term bearish read that the bounce has little room; our down leg needs a close back above $67,627 to end. Preview only, so its evidence was not read.

items.title: Market update - November 20th, 2026
items.points: Sees $60,000 as the key psychological level, with a base-case range of $60,000–$90,000, and rejects calls for $40,000; the October FOMC minutes were hawkish, with a 25 bp hike in December the central case; the IBIT bid-ask spread widened to about 17–19 bp.
items.meaning: The bottom of its range, $60,000, is where our order book shows the largest bid ($214M, Hyperliquid perps) and also a negative-gamma strike; the close has held above it for three days.

items.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
items.points: 13F filers added a net 49,229 BTC-equivalent in Q3 and hold a record 356,491, or 27.6% of spot BTC fund holdings; advisors and wealth platforms account for 40.5% of that. After quarter-end, fund holdings fell by 38,531 BTC through Nov 16.
items.meaning: The wealth-management clients who entered in Q3 have a cost near $80K and are now all underwater; by our estimate the close is 22.5% below the ETF holder cost basis, under it for 12 days. Last week's record outflows show some of them are already redeeming.

items.title: Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?
items.points: ETFs took in a net $6.36B in Q3 at a flow-weighted entry of about $78,300; it looks to $69,400 and $72,700 only after three straight days of ETF inflows and STH-SOPR back at 1.
items.meaning: We see none of its conditions for strength yet: ETFs are still in outflow and STH-SOPR is 0.983, below 1 for 18 days.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Capitulation Meets Support
items.points: $62–66K holds about a fifth of short-term holder coins; a daily close below $62K points to $58.5K and the realized price of $53.7K; MARA and Riot sold about 28K BTC in November.
items.meaning: Written before the break. The $62–66K it treated as support is now the wall overhead, and Monday's first retest was turned back; its miner-selling figure points the same way as today's second finding. No newer issue is on the listing.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC fell below the 200-week MA, ETF exposure is back to mid-August levels and funding is negative; it notes these readings have coincided with BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: Of its three pieces of bottom evidence, funding has already reversed: 4.78% today, positive on all three large venues. No newer issue is on the listing.

cards.dawn: Leaning bullish long term: heat fell from mid-range into the Midnight bottom zone within a month, and every past stretch here was higher a year on; the weekly score flips bearish in 2 more weeks.
cards.avgd: Bullish on value: the distance below the nine cost lines slid further into the low end of history this week; past bear lows went near 5 and this cycle's 11.7 low still holds. Cheap zone, not a bottom.
cards.p20: Bullish: no top in sight. Price would need about $110,776 to touch the 0.75 line; Pi Cycle and the top radar sit low and Tidemark leans to the bottom side, so the open question is how deep the low goes.
cards.lthloss: Leaning bullish, on the edge: the long-term holder loss share eased off its 11/20 cycle high and stays in the past bear-bottom range; a close under about $58,500 would set a new high and break the pattern.
cards.cyccmp: Neutral: on day 413 after the top this drawdown is barely past half of what past cycles showed on the same day, all below −75%; a shallow cycle means the old bottom timetable does not transfer.
cards.levels: Bearish: price sits under the true market mean and the ETF buyers' cost, with several averages and the short-term holder cost packed at $72K–$74K overhead; below, the next line is the realized price at $53.1K.
cards.urpd: Bearish near term: the thick supply cluster at 62–64K sits right overhead and today's push into it was sold back; this week's coins moved mostly at a loss, and only a close above 64K clears that wall.
cards.strike: Neutral: the year-end max pain sits above with weak evidence of pull; the nearer markers are the $60,000 put pile and $80,000 call pile, and negative gamma below spot would amplify a break under 60K.
cards.legs: Bearish: this down leg's deepest drop already exceeds most of the last 12 declines, and today's bounce stalled below the $63,750 volume node; it only turns into an up leg on a close at $67,627.
cards.pullback: Bearish: three pullback lights have been on together for 24 days, and past runs like this had a negative 90-day median; selling pressure is maxed and the bottom combo is set, but two lights must go out first.
cards.profit: Bullish, contrarian: nearly all short-term holders are underwater, and after losses topped 60% BTC rose 12 of 16 times over 30 days; their average cost near $71,861 means break-even selling on the way up.
cards.sopr: Bearish: short-term holders have sold at a loss for nearly three weeks, the deepest day went below the 10/30 dip, and clustered loss-taking is on day 14; SOPR back above 1 marks the handover done.
cards.rpl: Bearish: the one-year ratio is in past cycles' bottom zone, but the last 7 days booked about 7 times more loss than profit and the ratio hugs its low; past lows held only after a rebound to 0.76.
cards.miners: Bearish: price is under the $66,605 power break-even for mainstream rigs while hashrate still rose this week and difficulty is set to climb; a drop below the $59,412 production cost would force selling.
cards.etf: Bearish: this ETF outflow run equals about 21,000 BTC, 11.9 times what miners produced, and the 20-day sum is in an outflow stretch; with price under Strategy's cost, institutions are not absorbing supply.
cards.pr-us: Neutral: net of USDT, US buying matches offshore; the negative premium is almost all USDT trading below $1. Asia's OTC premium runs high, and US spot has not joined until the premium turns positive.
cards.ad: Bearish: new demand lags coins going dormant, spot and perp demand both shrink, stablecoins fell 5.96% in a month and realized cap inflows stopped 10 days ago; no new money backs a bounce until 30-day demand turns up.
cards.whale: Bearish: both whale tiers are shrinking this month and sped up this week, long-term holders have been net sellers for 111 days and coins keep moving to short-term hands; bounces meet supply until that reverses.
cards.svd: Bearish: OKX spot shows net taker selling over 7 days; the last day and 24 hours turned to buyers, but large orders still sell and only mid-size ones buy. Spot catches up only when the 7-day sum flips.
cards.stk: Bearish: US stocks rallied hard today while BTC closed flat, extending two months of lagging the S&P 500, Nasdaq and gold; the 2-year yield sits above the Fed cap and markets price a 97% hike chance.
cards.fh: Neutral: funding is positive but low, so longs are not crowded; perp longs chased today, yet open interest is down over a month and longs were 75% of liquidations. A move to 30% or below zero gives direction.
cards.vol: Neutral: implied volatility is high for the year, rich to realized and inverted at the front, so the market pays up for a big near-term move; direction rests on whether 64K or the 58.5K low breaks first.
cards.oi: Bearish: money is positioned for downside, with buyer premium tilted to puts for 26 days and puts priced richer in the risk reversal; the year-end max pain at $72,000 has little pull, protection dominates.
cards.fng: Bearish: sentiment has sat in extreme fear for a while after a neutral reading a month ago; past drops into this zone rose only 4 of 16 times over 30 days, and the fear is not digested until it climbs back above 25.
